blocks.content: The law assists only those who are vigilant, not those who sleep upon their rights.

rows: No power to extend prescribed period
Power to extend if 'sufficient cause' is proven
Right to appeal barred unless delay condoned

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Limitation Act, 1963 bars the judicial remedy after the prescribed period expires, without extinguishing the underlying right (except under Section 27).
Section 3 imposes a mandatory duty on courts to dismiss time-barred suits, even if limitation is not pleaded as a defense by the opposing party.
Section 5 allows condonation of delay for sufficient cause, but it is strictly applicable to appeals and applications, not to suits.
Under Section 12, the day from which the period of limitation is to be reckoned is excluded from the calculation.
Section 5 (Condonation of Delay) applies exclusively to appeals and applications; it NEVER applies to suits.
Under Section 3, the court is bound to dismiss a time-barred suit suo motu even if the defendant fails to raise limitation as a defense.
Section 27 is an exception to the general rule: it extinguishes the right to property itself after the expiry of the limitation period.
